title: Why MLPs Struggle with Images
description: Understand the parameter explosion and loss of 2D spatial locality when flattening image pixels into standard MLPs.

slides.title: The Flaw of Flattening Pixels 🖼️
slides.content:
# Why MLPs Fail on Vision

When feeding an image into a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), the 2D pixel grid $(H \times W \times C)$ is flattened into a 1D vector.

### The Two Fatal Flaws of MLPs on Images:
1. **Destruction of 2D Spatial Locality:** Pixels that are vertically adjacent in physical reality become separated by thousands of indices in a 1D vector. An MLP treats neighboring pixels identically to pixels on opposite corners of the screen.
2. **Parameter Explosion:** A modest $256 \times 256$ RGB image has $196,608$ input values. Connecting this to a single hidden layer with 1,000 neurons requires nearly **200 million weight parameters** for that single layer alone!

slides.title: MLPs vs Convolutional Neural Networks ⚖️
slides.content:
# Comparing Vision Architectures

| Feature | Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) | Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Spatial Topology** | Destroys 2D grid structure by flattening | Preserves 2D/3D spatial arrangement $(C, H, W)$ |
| **Parameter Count** | Explodes quadratically with image resolution | Drastically reduced through shared local weight kernels |
| **Translation Invariance**| None (must relearn cat features in every pixel position) | High (shared kernel detects features anywhere in image) |
| **Receptive Field** | Global connection to every input pixel | Localized receptive field expanding deeper in the network |
| **Hardware Efficiency**| Heavy memory bandwidth for dense matrices | Highly parallelized sliding dot products optimized for GPUs |

CNNs exploit spatial locality and translation invariance through shared local kernels

quizData.explanation: CNNs use shared weight kernels sliding across local pixel patches, preserving 2D spatial relationships and drastically reducing parameters.

slides.title: Defining a 2D Convolution in PyTorch 🐍
slides.content: A minimal 2D convolutional layer processing image batches in PyTorch:
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Batch of 4 RGB images, 3 channels, 32x32 pixels
images = torch.randn(4, 3, 32, 32)

# 3 input channels, 16 feature maps, 3x3 kernel, padding=1
conv_layer = nn.Conv2d(in_channels=3, out_channels=16, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
feature_maps = conv_layer(images)

print('Input batch shape: ', images.shape)
print('Output feature map shape:', feature_maps.shape)

slides.title: AI Pro Tip: Inductive Bias 💡
slides.content:
## Spatial Inductive Bias
Machine learning models succeed when their architectural assumptions match the problem domain.

CNNs possess a built-in **spatial inductive bias**: the prior assumption that nearby pixels interact strongly and that semantic patterns (like an eye or wheel) are invariant to spatial translation.
